PASS.head: ru
PASS.challenge: Most frequent class; a century of route outcomes consistent with the reading. Nothing verifies that 'sanctioned' is in the record rather than in HEL

THRU.head: ke
THRU.gloss: leg of a forced multi-node path
THRU.challenge: Validated by the broken-half method; 'forced' is inferred from the absence of a co-attested direct edge, not stated

SHUNT.head: tu
SHUNT.challenge: May be one class with RECUR, split by the 1908 consolidation (A §4.6a)

BAR.head: pe
BAR.gloss: edge present in the graph, not traversable in this orientation
BAR.challenge: Secure against IMP since the 1948 revision

RECUR.head: ha
RECUR.gloss: return to a similar but non-identical coordinate
RECUR.challenge: May be one class with SHUNT (A §4.6a)

BIND.head: si
BIND.gloss: co-incidence: same coordinate under two descriptions; not motion
BIND.challenge: No expedition outcome distinguishes a true BIND claim from a false one

ADJ.head: yu
ADJ.challenge: May be a nineteenth-century damage convention, not a class (A §4.6c). No head half has ever been recovered; yu- is derived by rule

in.challenge: 'Endpoint of the chain' vs 'endpoint of the record' is not distinguishable

is.challenge: Validated jointly with THRU; almost never independently testable

ar.meaning: other edges attach here, not stated
ar.challenge: May mark that the record is incomplete here (Hallam 1976, A §4.6b)

ol.challenge: 'Referenced' imports a referring act; nothing operational turns on OFF

ti.challenge: A modeled traversal produces no outcome to correlate against

ka.meaning: staged; conditions being brought into place
ka.challenge: The Archive's paraphrase of a contrast, not of anything the corpus states

lan.challenge: Performative ('I hereby authorize') vs stative ('in an authorized state'); Field Protocol restricts speaking AUTH forms near an active locus

kas.challenge: Best-correlated grade; completed vs in-progress is not recoverable

mun.meaning: the edge does not exist in the graph

sen.meaning: the edge exists and is traversable, and is closed
sen.challenge: By whom or by what is not stated; the Instrument school reads 'gated'

nir.meaning: exists, not closed, not available at this coordinate
nir.challenge: Whether dormancy is periodic, conditional or permanent is not stated

lus.meaning: this record does not establish the edge's status
lus.challenge: An asserted absence; conflated with wal UNW until 1948

he.meaning: polarity attaches to the edge pair, not the segment
he.challenge: Function inferred from the ambiguity its absence produces elsewhere

lar.challenge: Utterance: performed without entitlement. Instrument: recorded with the permission bit clear. Glossed dual-read at point of use; no first-person paraphrase

ro.challenge: No outcome distinguishes a spent grade from a lapsed one

lun.meaning: the grade remains in force; no release recorded
lun.challenge: Performative (in force until remitted) vs stative (a lifetime flag). AUTH-STANDING with no attested release is the Open Register

ki.meaning: in force under a condition the record does not state
ki.challenge: The condition is never stated; the value is known only by contrast

sar.challenge: Distinguished from SPENT by paradigm position only

le.meaning: discharge not stated, and the record says so
le.challenge: Formally clean; the overt-gap principle applied to discharge

li.meaning: the polarity holds at this pass
li.challenge: Edges closed ONCE have been found open on later passes

kur.meaning: the polarity holds at every recurrence
kur.challenge: No EVERY-closed edge has been found open; absence of a counterexample

ra.challenge: An explicit negative value; cannot be validated

nes.challenge: Formerly glossed 'registered by the system itself'; struck 1949

tir.challenge: The most human-shaped warrant; Instrument reads a sensor-provenance field

lekur.challenge: The lekur-alone rule: never translated with 'because'

hos.challenge: An inferred route successfully traversed confirms the route, not the inference

wal.challenge: Rests entirely on contrast with the other four; conflated with lus until 1948

[41].meaning: a sixth unit in the warrant slot; no sound value assigned
[41].challenge: Transmitted, not analyzed. Never eliminated as a copyist's artifact. Must not be explained

sa.challenge: Correlates with records HEL can independently date to one traversal

to.challenge: The one ordering claim operational records can check

nu.challenge: Indistinguishable from a default written when a field was not filled

kihar.meaning: at the anchor; no displacement stated

pukal.meaning: displaced ahead of the anchor, measured; the magnitude is not in the record

rolun.meaning: displaced behind the anchor, measured; the magnitude is not in the record

hilun.meaning: this slot is unfilled, and the record says so
hilun.challenge: 'Unknown to the record' vs 'withheld by the record' has never been settled
